extraction.Name: Henry Clifford
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want same, as he did not want to pay taxes; but that he was told, if he did not take the patent, and pay his taxes, it would be taxed just the same, and later sold for taxes, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold his land to Clements Valandry, of Rosebud, South Dakota, for $600.00, Valandry paying $300.00 in cash, and a Ford automobile, valued at $300.00
extraction.Buyer: Clements Valandry, of Rosebud, South Dakota, for $600.00 ($300.00 in cash and a Ford automobile valued at $300.00)
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms his father's land and works for outside farmers for his living, these two sources of income being all he has
extraction.NOTES: 160 acre allotment, NE, Sec. 30, T. 41N., R. 43W., 6th P.M., South Dakota; mentally competent and has good health; has a wife to support, who has good health; did not sell land for any debts incurred prior to receipt of patent in fee; on August 29, 1928, injured his hand badly in an automobile accident and was unable to work; United States Government issued rations starting December 1, 1928; as of April 8, 1929, rations were stopped though deponent states his hand not sufficiently recovered for hard work; considers he got a fair price for his land; affidavit sworn April 8, 1929 in Shannon County, South Dakota
